capabilities._note: Text to image only: no reference images.

template._note: Sizes a series ref is generated at (as krea2's). A keyframe is generated at its shot's render size, scaled up (same aspect, multiples of size_multiple) to at least min_pixels: the video targets scale a keyframe to the frame anyway, and Z-Image draws poorly far below its 1 MP training size.

recipe._note: Series refs are worded as krea2 words them (targets/image/common.py). Keyframes: targets/image/common.py keyframe_prompt.

binding._note: An API graph built from the user's saved z-image-turbo-t2i.json (ComfyUI's Z-Image Turbo template: UNETLoader + CLIPLoader lumina2 + ae VAE, ModelSamplingAuraFlow, KSampler res_multistep / simple, 8 steps, cfg 1). The saved canvas' LoRA loader is left out (references follow the series config's look; `loras` splices one in after the UNETLoader when asked). Every node the binding names has a title. H3SaveRefTake takes the place of SaveImage; prune drops anything it doesn't need. Known by the h3pipe_ name among ComfyUI's saved workflows, so the user's own canvas never leaks in.

models._note: Families from the installed files' headers (targets/modelid.py): Z-Image base and Turbo share their tensors, so Turbo is told by name. All required.

presets._note: ComfyUI's Z-Image Turbo template (image_z_image_turbo.json): 8 steps, cfg 1, res_multistep, shift 3 (the user's saved copy says 5). The negative prompt is the saved workflow's; at cfg 1 there is no guidance, so it has no effect (a take says so when one is set).

final.negative: low quality, bad anatomy, extra digits, missing digits, extra limbs, missing limbs

downloads._note: URLs from ComfyUI's image_z_image_turbo.json template (properties.models); the user's saved z-image-turbo-t2i.json has the same.
